tasks.short: Select vehicle-glass tools, protective equipment and parts

steps.what: Inspect the vehicle glass, fittings, damage and sensor arrangement to establish replacement or repair requirements
Look up applicable glass, moulding, adhesive and tool requirements in the vehicle-glass parts and repair-information category of {OTHER}
Select appropriate tools, safety equipment and parts; physically check glass features, adhesive suitability, protective gear and tool condition against the repair requirements

tasks.design: Test native vehicle-configuration filters and bookmarks in the repair-information category of {OTHER}. They shorten navigation to applicable glass and adhesive instructions while the technician checks the actual vehicle and selects the physical items.
tasks.previous_blocker: A vehicle variant can require searching several catalogue and repair-information sections.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing structured vehicle identifiers and document indexing can narrow navigation without interpreting repair suitability.
tasks.still_hard: Sensor fittings, glass options, adhesive conditions and safe tool condition must be checked on the job.
tasks.human_edge: The technician matches instructions to the actual glass and surrounding trim.

ambition.what: No new decision rights or service is assumed.

tasks.altitude: A small reduction in catalogue navigation; physical selection is unchanged.

reach.task: Establish whether replacement glass affects sensor calibration
reach.learn: Recognise calibration requirements and hand work to an authorised specialist.

evidence.claim: Vehicle identifiers and option filters can narrow a parts catalogue, but physical glass features still need verification.

assumptions: Boundary is selection only, excluding ordering, fitting, calibration and repair completion records. No separate report, send or stock transaction is required by this statement and none is invented.

The technician reads and checks vehicle identification, model year, body variant, visible glass options and sensors in s1; any identifier entry and catalogue verification are counted in s2. The repair-information provider supplies applicability, part code, adhesive specification and tool requirements. Missing options mean manual catalogue lookup and physical verification.

Test native filters first. The assumed saving is navigation only, not reading or interpreting safety instructions, and never software runtime. Shares are a provisional scenario, not measured baseline data.
unknowns: How often vehicle option records disagree with the actual glass
research_questions: Does a technician repeat navigation that the native configuration can remove?

already_counted.description: Catalogue applicability checks remain in s2.

incremental.description: Keep procedure bookmarks current and report mismatched applicability.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: An unconfigured catalogue gives 20 times 20 percent, or 4 gross hours, less 1 upkeep for 3 net. If filters already work, navigation benefit is zero. Inspection, instruction interpretation and physical equipment selection retain their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Same repair authority with slightly quicker reference access.
reach: Recognise jobs needing a calibration specialist.
role.ambitious_version: A glass technician who traces every selected part and tool to the actual vehicle configuration.
